units.translation: The verb, as H. Stephanus noted, is properly said of those who, after committing some murder, cut off the extremities of the slain and, fastening them together, carried them under the armpit: hence it is used of any more cruel slaughter, as of the slaughter of Agamemnon Ch. 439 ἐμασναλίσθη δ᾽, ἔθ᾽ ὡς τόδ᾽ εἰδῇς [he was mutilated, so that you may know this].
he was mutilated, so that you may know this
armpit-strap
armpit-strap
He threw the armpit-straps around his sides.
to act or think vainly
to act or think vainly
But the heart, whirling in eddies, does not act vainly (Karsten: πλαγκτὰ [wandering]).
vain, rash
vain, rash
A penalty is inflicted by a vain tongue.
Dare, O vain one.
In vain and wild snortings.
Of the vain thoughts of men.
With vain joy.
Every remedy is vain. Thus Musgrave for παμμάταιον [utterly vain].
Opinions bringing vain favor.
Vain miseries
A vain tongue.
Do not honor these vain howlings.
In the vain fortunes of masters.
A vain fear from the nights.
The eye of a man is not vain, where I corrected to μάταιον ἂν τόδ᾽ ὄψανον πέλοι [would this eye be vain].
Those who are vain in their own deeds.
Do not cast to the ground the fruit of a vain tongue.
Let what is not vain come from prudent faces.
Nor even in Hades, having died, will he escape the charges of vain things (thus Schuetz for μάταιον [vain]).
Of vain and unholy beasts.
Matallus, a Persian proper name
Matallus, a Persian proper name
to act idly or in vain
to act idly or in vain
This deed is being accomplished and does not act in vain.
Those whom I trust not to act in vain on the road.
Let us see if anything of this prelude acts in vain.
Doric for μάτην, which see
Doric for μάτην, which see
in vain
to seek, track
to seek, track
The stranger seems to be a keen tracker like a dog, seeking the murder she will discover.
We seek no prophets, which Schuetz restored for μαστεύομεν [we seek], since this form is constant in the remaining places of Aeschylus.
Do not seek another friend more than me.
A just lament seeks everything.
I also seek you.
error
error
fault, sin
They seek to take the exile by force with bloody errors.
But speak likewise also of your father's errors.
in vain, rashly
in vain, rashly
Why do you delay and lament in vain?
Do not toil in vain over things that help nothing.
Nor is it possible for me to speak with charming tongue in vain.
For in vain, helping nothing, you will toil for me.
Seeing, they saw in vain.
Not wishing to babble in vain.
So that she may know that she does not hear me in vain.
You trouble me in vain.
Speaking, I seem to say many things and in vain.
In vain the many missiles came.
They made many Persian women in vain bereft and husbandless.
If the burden of vain care must truly be cast off.
